```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pcaLab)
```

## Cellwise contamination

Modern wide data can contain a few bad cells in many rows. With enough variables, almost every row may contain at least one contaminated cell. This differs from classical casewise contamination.

```{r}
s <- pca_simulate(n=120,p=20,rank=3,cellwise=.03,seed=5)
```

If `cellWise` is installed:

```{r eval=FALSE}
fit <- pca_fit(s$data,method="cellwise",scale=TRUE,ncomp=3)
fit$extra$cellwise_map
fit$extra$rowwise_flags
```

The MacroPCA backend combines missing-value handling with rowwise and cellwise robustness. Backend-specific cell flags are preserved rather than converted into unverified generic outlier scores.
